findings.basis: Per-network false entries in Qualcomm vendor.xml carrier config overlays of LineageOS device trees: Fairphone FP4/FP5 (KPN 204-08/204-69, Telenet 206-05, BASE 206-20, Free 208-15/208-16, Telia NO 242-02, OneCall 242-05, 1&1 262-23, FET 466-01/02/03), Sony loire/nile (Bell 302-610/630/640), and many Sony trees with spn JAZZTEL on 214-03 (the two Jazztel profiles carry no family in the input; the evidence index points them to a Pixel marlin/sailfish baseline and the Sony overlays carry the JAZZTEL false entry). These are real shipped values, but for a different stack: on those Qualcomm devices the IMS client sits in the modem, so a 'CS' emergency dial from the framework still reaches the modem's own IMS/CS domain selection. On this phone ImsStack runs on the AP and the Samsung modem gets no IMS state (no IRadioIms, modem study lines 47-67 and 264), so 'CS first' here means CS only. The basis therefore does not carry over to this ROM and stack. The Google lane does not set the key for these SIMs, so Android's default true is served otherwise.
findings.effect: Path used by this ROM: the AOSP domain selection service is off. PhoneGlobals.java:520-525 builds DomainSelectionResolver from config_domain_selection_service_component_name, which is empty in packages/services/Telephony/res/values/config.xml:393 and is not overlaid by device/samsung or vendor/lineage; isDomainSelectionSupported() is false when the component is null (DomainSelectionResolver.java:139-146). The phone's dumpsys confirms 'DomainSelectionResolver created: componentName=[]' on LineageOS 24.0 (modem study, line 264). The local tree is named lineage-23.2-x1s but its manifest tracks lineage-24.0 / android-17.0.0_r1 and vendor/lineage/config/version.mk says 24.0, so it matches the phone. In this legacy path the key is read only in GsmCdmaPhone.useImsForEmergency() (GsmCdmaPhone.java:1243-1252): key && ImsService ready (ImsPhone.isImsAvailable() -> isImsServiceReady(), no IMS registration needed) && TTY allows VoLTE. dial() sets useImsForEmergency = isEmergency && useImsForEmergency() (:1337). An emergency call goes to IMS if either useImsForCall (IMS registered for MMTEL voice and VoLTE/WFC enabled, :1235-1241, ImsPhone.java:2544) or useImsForEmergency is true (:1422-1424). If the IMS dial throws, it falls back to CS (:1433-1437); if ImsStack fails the emergency call it reports CODE_LOCAL_CALL_CS_RETRY_REQUIRED with EXTRA_CODE_CALL_RETRY_EMERGENCY by default (EmergencyStartErrorHandler.cpp:139-140) and Telephony redials on CS (ImsPhoneCallTracker.java:3641-3667, Phone.java:847-876). The same useImsForEmergency() gates the CS-to-IMS retry when the modem answers a CS emergency call with EMC_REDIAL_ON_IMS or EMC_REDIAL_ON_VOWIFI (GsmCdmaCallTracker.java:1319-1332, 1449-1459). So with false: while IMS is registered for voice and the user has VoLTE/WFC on, the emergency call still goes over IMS (no change). In every other state (IMS not registered for this SIM: no VoLTE entitlement, registration failed or lost, VoLTE switched off by the user, roaming without VoLTE, limited service, TTY without TTY-over-VoLTE) the call goes to CS only, and a modem 'redial on IMS' cause is ignored.
findings.risk: With false instead of the default true, an emergency call placed while IMS is not registered for voice is never tried over IMS (neither IMS emergency registration on LTE nor over Wi-Fi). It depends entirely on the modem finding a CS cell. On networks and in countries without 2G/3G (Taiwan has switched off 2G and 3G, which affects all three FET profiles; 1&1's own network is LTE/5G only) the CS attempt can fail outright, and the modem's redial-on-IMS cause is dropped because the same gate is false. Elsewhere the call is delayed by the move from LTE to a 2G/3G cell. The Wi-Fi-only case (no cellular coverage, Wi-Fi calling registered but switched off, or registration lost) loses its only path. No case was found where false is safer than true on this stack, because the true path already falls back to CS when IMS fails.

notes: Hold. On LineageOS 24.0 with the AOSP ImsStack and domain selection off, the key decides whether Telephony tries IMS for an emergency call whenever IMS is not registered for voice. The false value comes from Qualcomm device overlays where the modem's own IMS still handles a CS emergency dial. On this phone that does not happen, so false removes the IMS attempt and the IMS retry. It can leave an emergency call with no working domain on LTE-only networks such as FET in Taiwan. Keep serving the Google lane / Android default (true) for all 17 profiles.
